patches.value: At finite scale every nonempty cover member has finite ediam, equal to the embedding of its real diam. Since p>0, zero diameter has p-power zero; the supremum over a nonempty-member proposition is exactly that diameter power, and for an empty member it is zero. Thus the infimum in D004 is precisely the original ordinary-diameter infimum H^p_δ, and F002 identifies μH[p] with the original H^p with no factor. Any countable subfamily, or the pairs (i,j) with i∈ℕ and 0≤j<N_i for a natural-number family N, has a countable index set: it is a subset of ℕ or ℕ×ℕ. Inject it into ℕ, place each set at its assigned index, and use ∅ elsewhere. The union is unchanged and each nonzero cost occurs once; the sum, defined as the supremum of finite subsums, is unchanged. These conclusions, F002 and F003 hold for all the arbitrary objects. Discharge L1 into p>0 and universally quantify to obtain every clause of the asserted output.

For any positive target scale Δ and tolerance τ, set rTarget=min(1,Δ/2)>0 and εTarget=τ/(2·2^(q+2))>0. F005 gives a cover of diameter ≤2rTarget≤Δ and cost <2^(q+2)εTarget=τ/2<τ. N001, now in maxProd(X,ℝ) with its Borel structure and positive exponent q+1, yields μH[q+1](A×I)=0. This and F005 are the two clauses of the asserted output. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A,q; Δ,τ were arbitrary small-cover test values, not new hypotheses.

Infimizing the bound F007 over the admissible families gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I), using the ordinary-cost identification N001. If there is no admissible family the right side is ∞ and the same inequality holds. Thus the bound holds for every finite δ>0; take suprema over these scales and apply N001 at the positive exponents s and s+1 to obtain μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify the arbitrary X,A,s,δ. This proves both clauses of the asserted output, without adding any measurability or compactness premise.

Fix V and A⊆V. The inclusion A⊆univ V and M006 give dimH(A)≤dimH(univ V). M008 identifies the latter with finrank(V). This is a natural number and hence <∞ when embedded in [0,∞]; nonnegativity follows from the codomain of dimH. Thus 0≤dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞, including finrank(V)=0, where the inequalities force dimH(A)=0. Quantify V,A to obtain the asserted output.

By F001, d≥0, so either d>0 or d=0. F007 and F009 give ofReal(d+1)≤h in the respective exhaustive branches. F004 gives the reverse inequality, and F001 identifies dimH(A) with d. Thus dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1. If finrank(V)=0 then N004 gives d=0 and the same zero branch applies; no positive-dimensional ball was needed in N002 or N003. Discharge L1 and quantify V,A to prove the asserted output with precisely its stated nonempty compact premise.

For the explicit metric comparison fix arbitrary x,y∈Vn and real t,u, and write a=||x−y||₂≥0 and b=|t−u|≥0. The domain distance is max(a,b). The sum of squared coordinate differences in Wn splits into its first n coordinates and the last coordinate, so the target distance between T(x,t),T(y,u) is sqrt(a²+b²). Each of a² and b² is at most a²+b², while a²+b²≤2 max(a,b)²; taking nonnegative square roots yields
 max(a,b)≤sqrt(a²+b²)≤sqrt(2) max(a,b).
Thus the coordinate map and its inverse have Lipschitz constants sqrt(2) and 1 respectively. These finite constants are independent of E,n and the points. The formulas hold also at n=0, where a=0. This verifies the metric representation explicitly; F001–F003 supply the equivalence, exact image identification and dimension equality. Together they prove every clause of the asserted output, with the source Vn Euclidean throughout.
